title: System Design Case Studies — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: System design case studies for Rails engineers should be solved with Rails tooling in mind — not generic distributed systems that could be any stack. A URL shortener uses PostgreSQL for the mapping and Redis for hot lookups. A news feed at scale uses Sidekiq for fan-out and Redis sorted sets for the feed timeline. A chat system uses ActionCable over Redis pub/sub. A notification service uses Sidekiq with multiple queues and priority routing to APNs, FCM, and SendGrid. This page walks through five case studies with capacity numbers (mandatory — 'lots of users' fails the depth check), Rails-specific implementation decisions, and the trade-offs at each architectural inflection point — the same structure an interviewer at a Rails shop expects to hear.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: url-shortener, news-feed-design, chat-system, notification-service, file-upload-pipeline. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
